clue.text: In the centre of publicity about road

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: an ad is a piece of publicity
the M1 motorway, written as MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A billboard campaign put up in the middle of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, and setters write its number as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning surrounded by or among, positioned in the middle of something.

clue.text: Dubliners see, they say, main part of the British Isles

definitions.text: main part of the British Isles

indicators.note: they say points to how a word is spoken rather than how it is written

blocks.note: people from Dublin are Irish
the verb, said out loud, matches the body of water

explanation.surface: Visitors from Dublin taking in the sights of most of Britain and Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Main is an old poetic word for the open sea, so 'main part' is a stretch of sea within the British Isles, not the bulk of the land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish Sea is the stretch of ocean lying between Great Britain and Ireland, so it is a watery portion of the isles.

clue.text: Colourist coming from Ryde

indicators.note: coming from suggests the letters emerge out of the town name in a new form

blocks.note: Ryde is a town on the Isle of Wight

explanation.surface: An artist who hails from the seaside town of Ryde.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer works with pigments to tint fabrics, making a trade colourist.

clue.text: Substitutes for braces in Arctic regions?

definitions.text: Substitutes for braces in Arctic regions?

blocks.note: surface reading: something to hold trousers up instead of straps over the shoulders
setter's reading: a brace is a pair, and in polar cold the pair one might have would be frozen rounds of ice

explanation.walkthrough: A brace means a pair, as in a brace of pheasants; the question mark flags the playful, slightly cheeky leap to balls of ice in freezing places.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice-balls are frozen spheres, the sort of pair one would find in polar cold, standing in for a brace.

clue.text: Appeal to petition the Queen

blocks.note: to pray is to petition or beseech
Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher

explanation.surface: Someone submitting a formal plea to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an earnest request or plea, the noun sense of an appeal.

clue.text: Gather around silver collection

indicators.note: around means the first word encloses the next one

blocks.note: to assemble is to gather together
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Collectors gathering round a display of silverware.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a group of things or people brought together, much like a gathered set.

clue.text: One politician with skill to communicate

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
Member of Parliament
art as in a craft or knack

explanation.surface: A politician gifted at getting the message across.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart is to pass on or convey information, which is what communicating does.

clue.text: An afterthought on the way led to attention-seeking sound

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: a postscript added at the end of a letter
street, abbreviated

explanation.surface: Remembering something extra while walking, then hissing to catch someone's ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the whispered noise made to draw someone's notice discreetly.

clue.text: Trespass inside my precinct, having had a drop too much

definitions.text: having had a drop too much

indicators.note: inside means one piece goes within another's boundaries

blocks.note: to trespass in the old biblical sense is to sin or go astray
the bounds of the word my, its precinct, are entered

explanation.surface: A drunk wandering onto private grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Precinct means an enclosed area; here it is the space between the two letters of my.
explanation.definitionFit: Merry is a mild British euphemism for slightly drunk or tipsy after drinking.

clue.text: Season that has its charms, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words could be arranged some other way

blocks.note: the letters used as they stand

explanation.surface: A wistful remark about a time of year with its own appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the festive season in late December, often called simply the season.

clue.text: Dries out with efficiency in the preferred way

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order

blocks.note: the letters used as they stand
done competently, an adverb

explanation.surface: Laundry drying out efficiently, just as one would want.
explanation.definitionFit: Desirably is an adverb meaning in a manner that is wished for or most wanted.

clue.text: Praise former partner, a lieutenant

blocks.note: an ex is a previous spouse or lover
taken as written
standard military abbreviation

explanation.surface: Speaking warmly of an ex who was an army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt is to glorify or extol someone highly, a verb of lavish approval.

clue.text: Fool breaking into wail at the singing of carols

indicators.note: breaking into means one piece forces its way inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
an ass is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A clown howling along during the carol service.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassail is the old custom of going from house to house singing seasonal songs and drinking good health.

clue.text: Carol singers' stays?

blocks.note: first meaning: bands of street musicians who sing at Christmas
second meaning: periods of remaining or delaying

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it read as the corsets of carol singers; in fact the clue offers two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the traditional groups of Christmas street singers are called by this name, and delays or pauses are its plural noun too.

clue.text: Unusual act is noted by storyteller

indicators.note: unusual signals something out of the ordinary, so the letters fall in an odd order

blocks.note: the letters used as they stand

explanation.surface: A raconteur remarks on a strange performance.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdotist is someone who relates short amusing tales, a teller of yarns.

clue.text: Refunds are best in other words

indicators.note: in other words suggests putting the letters into a different form

blocks.note: the letters used as they stand

explanation.surface: A shopper's verdict that getting money back is the top option.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebates are sums paid back to a buyer, partial returns of money already spent.

clue.text: Scrap mad herds

indicators.note: mad means wild or crazy, so the letters run in a disordered way

blocks.note: the letters used as they stand

explanation.surface: A farmer ordering stampeding cattle to be got rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a small torn piece or fragment, just as a scrap is.

clue.text: Picture of one wise man

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a mage is a magus or sage

explanation.surface: A painting of one of the Magi at the Nativity.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a representation or likeness, such as a painting or photograph.

clue.text: Issue at the centre of the universe, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said aloud, not as written

blocks.clueFragment: at the centre of the universe
blocks.note: the star at the middle of our solar system

explanation.surface: A grand claim that one's child is the centre of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the centre of the universe' tempts a letter-selection from universe; it is a description of the star our planets orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal and formal word for offspring, so a male child counts.

clue.text: Narrow escape for the girl next door?

blocks.note: first meaning: a lucky avoidance of disaster
second meaning, playful: an unmarried young woman who lives close by, a nearby Miss

explanation.walkthrough: Miss is the title for an unmarried woman, and the girl next door is a close one, so the phrase splits as near plus Miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is an incident where an accident or collision is only just avoided.

clue.text: Some may equal target for sacrificial board

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used

blocks.note: found across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Planning a sacrifice to hit a target of equal size.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the table on which offerings to a deity are made, a board for sacrifice.

clue.text: Make a mistake in set-up around the dishes

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading the word from bottom to top
around means the turned word wraps round the other pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
to err is to go wrong
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook slipping up while laying out the serving plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-up' looks like a single noun, but it splits into set plus a reversal signal for a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrines are earthenware cooking pots, and also the pâtés cooked in them, so either way they are dishes.

clue.text: Walks a way, then takes transport

blocks.note: street, abbreviated
rides as in travels on a bus or horse

explanation.surface: A commuter walks part of the way, then catches a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Strides is a verb meaning moves along on foot with long steps.

clue.text: Crooks turn back in the streets of Paris

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction
in means the turned word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a go is a turn in a game
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: Criminals doubling back through Parisian streets to evade capture.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogues are dishonest scoundrels, much the same as crooks or villains.

clue.text: Still sent around the Italian

indicators.note: around means the first word encloses the next

blocks.note: taken as written
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian still being posted around the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Italian' is not a person but the Italian word for the.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent means making no sound, which is one sense of still, as in a still night.

clue.text: Scared when a few originally had hearing equipment

indicators.note: originally means taking what comes at the origin, the starting letters

blocks.note: the opening letters of each of these two words
having ears, the organs of hearing

explanation.surface: A few people were frightened when they found themselves wearing hearing aids.
explanation.definitionFit: Afeared is an old or dialect form of afraid, meaning frightened.

clue.text: It's dark near the junction

blocks.note: nigh is an old word for close by
a T-junction, shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A warning that the road junction ahead is unlit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: what is dark is the time after sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period of darkness each day, so a cryptic description of it is a thing that is dark.

clue.text: A Frenchman's Christmas

blocks.note: first meaning: a man's first name, common in France
second meaning: the festive season, from the French word for it

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it read as one man's holiday; the 's simply joins a French man's name to the festival that name also means.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a male given name in France and elsewhere, and is also a word for the Christmas season used in carols.

clue.text: Little darling hides fleeces

blocks.note: lamb is a term of endearment for a child
hides are animal skins

explanation.surface: A small child conceals something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hides' reads as a verb about the darling concealing things; it is the noun for animal pelts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambskins are the woolly pelts of young sheep, so they are fleeces.

clue.text: Precipitation at three points around a circle

indicators.note: around means the points are set on all sides of the round shape

blocks.note: three compass points: south, north, west
the letter shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A weather map with flakes falling at points round a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is frozen water falling from clouds, one form of precipitation alongside rain and hail.

clue.text: Stare endlessly at the sun, for instance

indicators.note: endlessly means without its ending, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning against gazing too long at the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun is the nearest example of a star, a glowing ball of gas in space.

clue.text: Flat anthems in ritual practices

blocks.note: even as in level or smooth
an anthem is a type of song

explanation.surface: Hymns sung off-key during church ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' tempts as a musical complaint about the anthems; it means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensongs are the regular evening services of the Anglican church, a set liturgical observance.

clue.text: The last of love is great

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O
mega is slang for great or huge

explanation.surface: A romantic insists the final stage of a love affair is wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the end of anything.
